strings.title: SERIAL_LOCK
strings.subtitle: LOCK 0x12 // CLASS: BURIED
strings.briefing:
Support staff paste invoice numbers into free text. The ref column holds 'Invoice INV-24359 paid', 'inv-11331' and '#INV-89275 (late)'. The number is always there, but never in the same place or the same case.

The lock wants exactly INV- followed by five digits, upper case. Extract it from the text, then deal with the status column, which has stray spaces and mixed casing.

df is loaded. 150 rows, 4 columns.
strings.task: The ref column hides an invoice number inside other text. Replace each ref with just the invoice number written as INV-12345 (upper case). Also make the status column lower case with no extra spaces.

starterCode.python:

df[['ref', 'status']].head(15)

python: Extract the id ignoring case: df['ref'].str.extract(r'(?i)(inv-\d{5})')[0], then .str.upper()
Status needs .str.strip() and .str.lower(). Assign each result back to its column.
sql: JavaScript-style patterns have no case-insensitive flag here, so spell it out: [Ii][Nn][Vv]-\d{5}
UPDATE data SET ref = UPPER(REGEXP_EXTRACT(ref, '([Ii][Nn][Vv]-\d{5})')), status = LOWER(TRIM(status));
